subject: Follow-up: CareOptics pilot — prompt samples, model recommendations, and redaction
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Dana Lee <dana@careoptics.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 25 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0400
Subject: Follow-up: CareOptics pilot — prompt samples, model recommendations, and redaction

Hi Dana — thanks again for the discovery today. Quick recap + concrete asks so we can scope the pilot: 

1) Goal: Verify Redwood inference fit for CareOptics’ triage assistant (clinical routing + short summaries) with emphasis on low-latency responses and PII-safe outputs.
2) Success metrics (your list): accuracy on intent routing >= 92%, median latency < 220ms for 256-token requests, no PII leakage in sampled outputs.

Next steps we discussed:
- You send 50–100 representative user prompts (de-identified if needed) and 10 flagged edge cases.
- We’ll run a 2-model benchmark (Redwood-opt-7b-quant, Redwood-opt-13b-int8) and return token-level cost/latency and a short quality report.
- Ben will propose batching/quantization settings after we see sequence-length distribution.

Practical items: please attach a CSV of prompt examples (column: prompt, context, expected_label) or paste them inline. If anything includes PHI you want retained, note that clearly and we’ll route to our Private deployment team.

I attached a simple CSV template and a short redaction checklist we recommend. If you prefer, procurement can attach sample data to a secure folder and we’ll pull from there (link below).

Thanks — aiming to get benchmark results in 3 business days after we receive the sample pack.

— Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0199

Attachments: CareOptics_prompt_samples.csv (template), redaction_guidance_v1.md
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Dana Lee <dana@careoptics.io>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 27 Jul 2026 09:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Follow-up: CareOptics pilot — prompt samples, model recommendations, and redaction

Folks — adding a few technical notes based on the discovery: 

- If CareOptics expects many short clinician queries (avg tokens <100) we’ll likely recommend Redwood-opt-7b-quant for cost/latency balance; however for longer-context summarization and specialty domain jargon the 13b-int8 reduces hallucination risk.
- For benchmark reproducibility please include: sequence length histogram, proportion of multi-turn context, and any must-not-emit tokens/phrases (PII patterns).
- We’ll run a prefix-KV cache experiment to measure cold vs hot-call latency; that’ll affect batching guidance.

Quality/regression guardrails: we can bind the evaluation to your prompt set and provide a small eval harness (unit tests + golden outputs) so future model swaps trigger alerts. If you want, Marissa can own the eval criteria and sample labeling.

Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

On the attachments, I recommend including 8–12 edge cases that are likely to include ambiguous role language (e.g., ‘nurse’ vs ‘RN’) and 3–4 prompts where the user intentionally includes PHI to validate redaction behavior.
From: Dana Lee <dana@careoptics.io>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@careoptics.io, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 08:41:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Follow-up: CareOptics pilot — prompt samples, model recommendations, and redaction

Thanks Tessa & Ben — this is helpful. We’ve pulled an initial pack and attached 60 de-identified prompts plus 12 flagged edge cases. A couple notes: 

- The dataset includes several verbatim patient quotes we redacted with [REDACTED_PATIENT] tokens; procurement attached a secure Drive folder with the original files per your guidance (link below).
- We also included a short list of unacceptable outputs (phrases that must not be returned). 

Can you confirm: where will these samples be stored during the benchmark run, and how long will Redwood retain them? We need confirmation for our security team before sharing the originals.

Dana
Dana Lee
Director of Product | CareOptics

Drive (procurement): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1CareOpticsSecureFolder
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Dana Lee <dana@careoptics.io>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 08:52:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Follow-up: CareOptics pilot — prompt samples, model recommendations, and redaction

Hi Dana — quick answers on retention/storage: 

- For the hosted benchmark we stage samples encrypted at rest in a scoped S3 bucket with 30-day retention by default; only the project team (Ben, Marissa, and the bench-runner service account) will have access.
- If you need, we can run the benchmark in your VPC (Redwood Private) so the raw unredacted files never leave your network — this is common for customers with PHI concerns.
- We also provide a signed evidence note (timestamped run logs + audit digest) that you can include in your vendor security review.

If procurement needs a short description for security review, I can draft one and copy the retention policy and audit link.

— Neha
Neha Kapoor
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Dana Lee <dana@careoptics.io>

Appreciate the fast answers. Procurement confirmed they’ll drop the originals into the secure Drive folder today and leave the de-identified CSV in this thread. We’d prefer a Private run if possible — please send the steps and an estimated cost delta for Private vs hosted benchmark.

Also: attaching a short CSV (CareOptics_prompt_samples.csv) with the sample prompts and a small README describing edge-case flags. Let me know if you need anything else.

Dana
